description: Effective manifest for fixtures derived from one recorded SIG capture. The hashes here describe the committed fixture bytes; replay tests verify against them. source-provenance.json is sanitized provenance derived from the capture manifest (not byte-exact); it keeps original hashes only for unmodified bodies and must not be used to validate redacted fixtures.

source_capture.provenance_label: sanitized source provenance derived from the capture manifest; NOT the byte-exact capture manifest

derivation.method: Unmodified fixtures are byte-identical copies of the recorded bodies. Redacted fixtures replace only the JSON value token at each listed path, byte-for-byte everywhere else; this was checked by comparing the Decimal-parsed original, with the listed replacements applied, against the parsed fixture.

a truncated sample: three pages of 50 trades, each with hasMore true, read over the fixed window [2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z, 2026-10-10T00:00:00.000Z). The 150 trades span 2026-10-09T09:43:11.765Z to 2026-10-09T22:33:16.692Z. The final page was not read; nothing is known about older trades in the window.

every trade's volume equals its side price (price for YES, 1 - price for NO) times size computed in binary floating point and printed in shortest form, so some values carry float noise (for example 0.7800000000000007). An observation about these 150 trades, not a client requirement or a documented contract.

coverage was present on every page with complete true; projectedThroughSequence differed between pages (133949521, 133950141, 133950511). These are kept as sent; they say nothing about whether SIG's reporting projection had caught up with the trading engine (projection freshness unknown).
